meta.title: The Best Dhikr App for iPhone in 2026 (Ranked)
meta.description: The best dhikr app for iPhone in 2026, ranked: QuranWall keeps an ayah on your Lock Screen, and six apps that count dhikr are compared from their live listings.

sections.title: Quick Answer
sections.content: The best dhikr app for iPhone in 2026 is **QuranWall**, if you want remembrance in front of you without opening anything: it puts an ayah of the Quran on your Lock Screen wallpaper and Home Screen widget, in Uthmani Arabic or a translation. It is not a tasbih counter; for counting, Dhikr & Dua, ZikrApp and Muslim Pro each include one, per their US App Store listings on 27 November 2026. QuranWall is our app, so it is ranked first; this is the honest case.

sections.text: Most people searching for the **best dhikr app for iPhone** (or the best zikr app, the other common spelling) want the same thing: to remember Allah more often, not just when they remember to open an app. That last part is the trap. A tasbih counter is only as good as your discipline in launching it, and by week two the icon can sit untouched on page three of your Home Screen. The apps below are ranked by one question: how well do they keep the remembrance of Allah present in your actual day?
What a dhikr app really needs to do

Dhikr means remembrance. So the job isn't counting — counting is the easy part your thumb can do. The hard part is being reminded to start. A great dhikr app has to close the gap between intention and action: it should surface remembrance where you already look, hold a morning-and-evening rhythm, and never demand that you dig through folders to begin. Judge every app on that, and the ranking sorts itself out fast.
The best dhikr apps for iPhone, side by side

Seven apps are compared here, and they split into two jobs. Four are built to count dhikr (Dhikr & Dua, ZikrApp, Dhikr App and Tasbih Counter Pro), and Muslim Pro and Athan include a counter inside a prayer app. QuranWall does the other job: it keeps an ayah of the Quran in view on the Lock Screen. Each row comes from that app's own listing.

| App | What it does for dhikr | Counter | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **QuranWall** (our app) | Keeps an ayah of the Quran on your Lock Screen wallpaper and widgets | No | Remembrance you see without opening an app |
| Dhikr & Dua | More than 500 duas and dhikr by category, with translation, transliteration and audio | Yes, per dhikr and stand-alone | A library to read and listen from |
| ZikrApp | Prayer-bead counting, a +1 button on the Lock Screen, a daily tracker and streaks | Yes | Counting and keeping a streak |
| Dhikr App | Voice counting, Bluetooth ring support, reminders and widgets | Yes | Hands-free counting |
| Tasbih Counter Pro | Saved dhikrs with targets, reminders and vibration alerts | Yes | A plain counter and nothing else |
| Muslim Pro | Duas and remembrance for daily moments inside a prayer and Quran app | Yes, built in | One app for prayer, Quran and dhikr |
| Athan (Islamic Finder) | Dua and athkar with audio, plus Daily Goals | Yes, built in | Prayer times first, dhikr second |

Read both tables as a snapshot, not a verdict: every fact comes from the app's own US App Store listing on 27 November 2026, ratings are rounded to one decimal, and listings change with each update. Two things stand out. QuranWall's listing is young and has two ratings so far, while Dhikr & Dua, Muslim Pro and Athan have thousands, so that gap is real. And the minimum iOS runs from iOS 15.0 to iOS 26.0, so check it before you pick.
The best dhikr apps for iPhone, ranked
QuranWall ranks first because it solves the reminder rather than the count. The six counting apps follow by how central dhikr is to each one, and every heading names the reader it suits best.
1. QuranWall — best for keeping an ayah in view (our pick)

QuranWall wins because it solves the reminder problem instead of the counting one. It places an ayah of the Quran directly on your **iPhone lock screen** wallpaper and Home Screen widget, in Uthmani Arabic or a translation, and the ayah stays put until you pick another in the app. Every time you pick up your phone, a verse is already there. No streak to babysit. You choose the background, font and colours, so the screen can suit your prayer or evening wind-down. For turning remembrance into something you *see* rather than something you have to schedule, it is the most direct fit on this list. That's why it ranks first as the **best dhikr app for iPhone** in 2026 — with one caveat: QuranWall shows Quran verses, it is not a tasbih counter.

sections.content: On iOS 16 or later, iOS can link a Lock Screen to a Focus (touch and hold the Lock Screen, then tap Focus). Link the one with your ayah to a Focus you run after Maghrib, and the Lock Screen becomes your cue for evening adhkar without a single notification.

sections.text: For the setup itself, see our guide to [putting a Quran verse on your iPhone Lock Screen](/blog/quran-verse-iphone-lock-screen). If reminders are your gap, we cover them in [how to set dhikr reminders on iPhone](/blog/how-to-set-dhikr-reminders-iphone), and QuranWall also topped our [best Islamic lock screen app roundup](/blog/best-islamic-lock-screen-app-iphone).
2. Dhikr & Dua — best for a library of duas with audio

Dhikr & Dua comes from Life With Allah, per its listing, and it is the most-rated dedicated dhikr app in this comparison. It holds more than 500 duas and dhikr sorted by category, each with a translation and a transliteration, and audio you can play one at a time or as a whole collection. Any dhikr meant to be repeated gets its own counter, and a stand-alone counter takes preset or custom targets. You can also pick a feeling, such as anxious or worried, and see the duas listed for it. It installs on iOS 15.0.
3. ZikrApp — best for counting on prayer beads and keeping a streak

ZikrApp's listing centres on the count itself: on-screen prayer beads with a different bead every 33, voice counting for some dhikrs, a mode that counts at a pace you set, and a +1 button on the Lock Screen, in the Dynamic Island and in Control Center. A daily tracker puts dhikr beside the five prayers and fasting, with targets and streaks. It reads morning and evening adhkar, tasbih after salah and surahs before sleep in order on one counter, and it runs group dhikr toward a shared goal. It comes in six languages (English, Russian, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Turkish and Indonesian) and installs on iOS 16.0 or later.
4. Dhikr App — best for hands-free counting

Dhikr App, listed on the App Store as Dhikr - Dua, Athkar & Tasbih, leads with counting by voice: you recite and its microphone feature keeps the count, which the listing pitches for driving, walking or any time your hands are busy. It also pairs with a Bluetooth counting ring. Around that sit reminders for daily adhkar and duas, a weekly Friday reminder for salawat on the Prophet (peace be upon him) and Surah Al-Kahf, streaks and statistics, Lock Screen and Home Screen widgets, a Siri Shortcut and 22 languages. The catch is the requirement: iOS 26.0, so older iPhones cannot install it.
5. Tasbih Counter Pro — best plain counter

If you want a counter and nothing else, this is the plain choice. Its listing describes saved dhikrs with a name, count, note, target and reminder, a count that resumes where you left off, vibration and sound alerts so you can count without looking, and counting by touching anywhere on the screen. It has a night mode and colour themes, comes in eight languages including English, Arabic, Turkish and Indonesian, and installs on iOS 15.1. The same developer also lists a Lite version.
6. Muslim Pro — best all-in-one with a built-in tasbih

Muslim Pro is a prayer and Quran app first: prayer times with adhan alerts, the Quran with audio, qibla, and a prayer and fasting tracker. For dhikr, its listing names a collection of duas and remembrance for specific moments, such as waking up, travelling and eating, plus a built-in tasbih counter. Choose it if you want one install for the whole day and are happy to open it on purpose; the counter waits inside the app until you do.
7. Athan — best if prayer times come first

Athan, listed under the developer name Islamic Finder, is built around prayer times and the adhan, with a prayer-times widget for the Home Screen. Its listing also names a tasbih counter, a dua and athkar section with audio, and Daily Goals that include completing a daily tasbih or dhikr. Keep it for the adhan; for dhikr it is a useful extra rather than the centre of the app.

Pillars, which an earlier version of this list named, is a prayer-times app with a prayer tracker and a Lock Screen widget for prayer times. Its listing on 27 November 2026 names no dhikr counter and no adhkar list, so it is no longer ranked here.
Where this gets hard

Here's the part nobody tells you about tasbih apps: **the habit often fades by week two.** Opening a counter is a habit, and habits that depend on you remembering to launch something fade fast. The same goes for screenshotting a verse and setting it as your wallpaper: you'll do it twice, then forget. QuranWall sidesteps both by designing the ayah for the surface you can't ignore, and changing it takes a few taps in the app. You don't need discipline to *look at your own Lock Screen*; you already do it all day.

sections.text: Read the ayah in Uthmani Arabic or in a translation in the language you think in, and the verse lands. Whichever you choose, the highest-leverage place for remembrance isn't inside an app you open twice — it's the screen you glance at all day. The Quran ties that assurance directly to remembrance.
Those who have believed and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of Allah. Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured.
How to set it up

items: Download QuranWall from the App Store.
Choose your translation language, then a background, font and colours: a preset or your own photo.
Pick an ayah and tap **Make It Mine** to set it as your Lock Screen wallpaper (Apple's Shortcuts app applies it), then add the QuranWall widget to your Home Screen.
Optional: on iOS 16 or later, link that Lock Screen to an iOS Focus you use for prayer or the evening.
If you count dhikr, keep one of the counter apps above beside it. Turn on auto-rotate and the QuranWall widget shows a new ayah daily, every 8 hours or hourly.

sections.content: A dhikr counter counts what you already remembered to do. A lock-screen verse reminds you in the first place. For most people, the reminder is the missing piece — not the counter.

sections.text: Frequently asked questions
Can QuranWall count my dhikr?

No. QuranWall has no dhikr or tasbih counter. It keeps an ayah of the Quran on your Lock Screen wallpaper and Home Screen widget, and the widget can show a new ayah daily, every 8 hours or hourly once you turn on auto-rotate. For counting, keep a counter app beside it, such as Dhikr & Dua, ZikrApp or Tasbih Counter Pro.
What is the best dhikr counter app for iPhone?

It depends on how you count. Of the apps read on 27 November 2026, Dhikr & Dua had the most US ratings among the dedicated dhikr apps and pairs its counters with a library of duas and audio. ZikrApp counts on prayer beads and from the Lock Screen, Dhikr App counts by voice on iOS 26, and Tasbih Counter Pro is the plain counter.
Which dhikr app has morning and evening adhkar?

Per the listings, ZikrApp reads morning and evening adhkar, tasbih after salah and surahs before sleep in order on one counter, and Dhikr App sets custom reminders for daily adhkar and duas. Muslim Pro's collection covers duas for set moments such as waking up and travelling. QuranWall does a different job: the ayah on your Lock Screen.
Will these apps run on an older iPhone?

Check the minimum iOS in the table first. QuranWall installs on iOS 15.0 or later, but its Lock Screen wallpaper and Lock Screen widgets need iOS 16; on iOS 15 you get the Home Screen widget. Dhikr & Dua and Muslim Pro install on iOS 15.0, Tasbih Counter Pro on iOS 15.1, Athan on iOS 15.6 and ZikrApp on iOS 16, while Dhikr App needs iOS 26.

So rank them honestly: keep a counter such as ZikrApp or Tasbih Counter Pro if you love logging reps, keep Muslim Pro or Athan for the adhan, and for weaving remembrance into a fuller day see our [Muslim morning routine setup](/blog/muslim-morning-routine-iphone). For the wider picture, see our [Muslim app guide for iPhone](/blog/best-muslim-app-for-iphone-2026). But the app that keeps the remembrance of Allah where you already look, on your Lock Screen, is QuranWall.
